lp.v: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’
lp.p: Pray for spiritual protection, hand over to God the temptations you may face today, and finish by giving the Kingdom, the power, and the glory to God.
lp.e: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever.

five.v: “Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted on the earth.”
five.p: Shut out the outside noise, take a deep breath, and let your heart come back from the rush to God. Focus on Jesus, not on yourself, other people, or circumstances.
five.e: Lord, I set everything down and am still before you.

five.v: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise. Give thanks to him, and bless his name.
five.p: Let God be God. Use praise to acknowledge that he is King and worthy of all the glory.
five.e: You are the King of kings, and you are worthy of all praise.

five.t: Confess and return to our proper place
five.v: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
five.p: Let us be human. Confess one way you left your proper place today and tried to be in charge.
five.e: I confess that today I tried to take control again. Please forgive me.

five.v: In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you.
five.p: Name three things you can thank God for today, even the small ones.
five.e: Thank you for a peaceful morning, my family’s smiles, and the opportunity to work.

five.v: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
five.p: Pray for your “2s,” and finally entrust yourself to God, saying: may your will be done.
five.e: I place my family, my coworkers, and my brothers and sisters in your hands, and I place myself in your hands too.

min.v: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
min.d: Be still for a few seconds and ask the Holy Spirit to search your heart: lay down the urge to perform, admit that you also need grace, and invite the Spirit to lead.
min.s: (In your heart) Lord, I am not doing this in my own strength. Please reign in me.

min.v: Jesus asked him, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him, “Rabboni, that I may see again.”
min.d: Ask open questions. Listen to what they say, to the heart they haven’t voiced, and to the Holy Spirit at the same time. Reflect back once to confirm.
min.s: “How would you like me to pray for you?” “What I’m hearing is…. Is that right?”

min.v: In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don’t know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can’t be uttered.
min.d: Pause quietly and ask the Holy Spirit what to pray for. If you sense something, share it humbly and test it against Scripture.
min.s: “I have a sense of something. It may not be exactly right, but see if it means anything to you…”

min.t: Pray in the name of Jesus
min.v: But Peter said, “I have no silver or gold, but what I have, that I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!”
min.d: Lay on hands (shoulder or head) only after asking permission. Pray briefly, clearly, and with faith. You can use Scripture.
min.s: “May I put my hand on your shoulder while I pray for you?”

min.v: ‘The LORD bless you, and keep you. The LORD make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. The LORD lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
min.d: Close with a blessing, then ask how they are feeling now, and give the glory to God together.
min.s: “How was that for you while we were praying? Let’s thank God together.”

min.v: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
min.d: Write down their needs and anything you promised, keep it confidential, and check in again in a few days. When needed, refer them to a pastor or professional help.
min.s: “I’ll keep praying for you over the next few days, and I’ll check in with you in a couple of days.”

rules: Keep the focus on Jesus
We are not trying to show people our spirituality, but to help them see Jesus.
Listen before you pray
Asking beats guessing. First understand what the person really needs.
Ask permission
Before praying for someone, laying on hands, or sharing what you sense, ask whether they are willing.
Respect physical boundaries
Place your hand only on the shoulder or head; have a companion present with someone of the opposite sex; get a parent’s consent for children.
Keep confidences
Never pass on prayer requests. To share one in a prayer meeting, first get the person’s permission.
No guarantees, no condemnation
Don’t say “You will definitely get better,” and don’t say “Your faith isn’t strong enough” or “It’s because you sinned.”
Respect medical care
Encourage people to keep seeing their doctor and taking their medication; medicine is also God’s grace. Never make medical decisions for anyone.
Share what you sense humbly
Use words like “I sense it might be…,” and test it against Scripture and the confirmation of spiritual companions.
Know when to refer
When there are thoughts of harming oneself or others, violence, or serious physical or mental health conditions, encourage professional help and inform a pastor.
Give the glory to God
Whatever the outcome, give the glory to Jesus and give thanks in everything.

s: Greetings and sharing
Each person shares, in a sentence or two, something they are thankful for this week and one prayer request.
Read a passage
Read a short passage together, such as this lesson’s key verse.
Worship and thanksgiving
Take turns praising and thanking God in one sentence each.
Pray for each other
Pray for each other’s requests. Each person can pray two rounds.
Bless one another
Bless each other with the blessing from Numbers 6.
Quiet your hearts
The leader invites everyone to be still, set aside their busyness, and turn their focus to Jesus.
Worship in song
Sing one or two songs, or read a psalm aloud together.
Scripture and theme
Read a passage and explain today’s prayer theme.
Confession and thanksgiving
Confess quietly, then take turns giving thanks in short sentences.
Pray around the theme
Take turns praying short prayers around the same theme, for two or three rounds.
Pray for one another
In groups of two or three, listen to one another and then pray for each other.
Declare and bless together
Say the Lord’s Prayer together and bless one another.
Worship
Worship in song, leading the congregation into God’s presence.
Message and vision
Give a short message on a passage and share the church’s prayer vision.
Confession and repentance
Confess quietly, and the leader prays briefly on behalf of the congregation.
Pray for the church
Pray for pastors, coworkers, members, and the next generation.
Pray for the city and nation
Pray for those in authority, the needs of society, and open doors for the gospel.
Pray for missions and the nations
Pray for missionaries, unreached peoples, and the persecuted church.
Pray for personal needs
Invite those with needs to stay behind, and have prayer team members minister in pairs.
Declaration and blessing
Say the Lord’s Prayer together, declaring that the Kingdom, the power, and the glory are God’s.

timer.p: Set aside what you are doing, take a deep breath, and turn your heart to Jesus.
Let God be God: praise him for who he is.

timer.t: Confess and return to our proper place
timer.p: Let us be human: confess where you have left your proper place.
Count God’s grace to you today.
Pray for your “2s,” and hand your needs to God.
Be still and listen for the Holy Spirit’s prompting.
